newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish February credit growth 15.5 pct y/yr - C.Bank.
newsitem.headline: Irish February credit growth 15.5 pct y/yr - C.Bank.

text.p: The adjusted annual rate of growth of Irish private sector credit rose to 15.5 percent in February from 15.2 percent in January, central bank monthly statistics showed on Thursday.

The absolute increase in private sector credit in February was of broadly similar magnitude to that in the same month of recent years although the increase this year was lowered somewhat by a fall in lending to the Agricultural Intervention Agency, the bank said.
Lending to the agency fell by 106 million Irish pounds in February while it was down by just 15 million at the same time last year.
It said the increase in non-government credit was entirely Irish-pound denominated and a sizeable proportion of the increase was due to mortgage lending.
Residential mortgage lending was moderately stronger in February than in the same month last year but the annual rate remained unchanged at 14 percent, the bank said.
Non-mortgage Irish-pound credit was fractionally weaker than February last year and the annual rate of increase slowed to 16.8 percent from 16.9 percent.
The central bank said there was a relatively large increase in the broad money supply in February but around half of this was due to exceptional items in the foreign currency component.
The adjusted rate of growth of M3E, the broad money supply measure, rose to 16.6 percent from 14.7 percent in January.
The increase in private sector credit was 145 million or 0.4 percent in February against 0.6 percent in February 1996, the bank said.
The rise was entirely Irish-pound denominated with foreign currency lending falling by seven million during the month.
Much of the increase was due to mortgage lending with residential mortgages increasing by 83 million Irish pounds and other mortgages up by 23 million.
There was also an increase of 65 million in term loans, the central bank said.
